constraint_decided_it: P177 assigned property of type (E13 -> E55) explicitly admits property types external to the CIDOC CRM (its own example: "'binding structure type' refers to a property, external to the CIDOC CRM"), and Issue 615 added "The property or relation need not be part of the CRM" to E13's scope note for v7.3.2. So E13 does have a structured home for a non-CRM assertion such as 'proportion of respondents opposed'. Neither answer's stated blocker survives: P14 carried out by (E7 -> E39, necessary 1,n) requires an actor for the *assertion*, which is the trust/consultation platform, not the respondents, and crm732#s0024 and #s0046 expressly contemplate knowledge-creation events whose creator is not identified, with responsibility then defaulting to the maintaining institution. Nothing in E13's scope note says 'single identifiable opinion-holder'.
better_modelling: Partially in scope. Consultation = E7 Activity, P14 carried out by the trust, P4 has time-span, P17 was motivated by the proposed road scheme; report = E31 Document, P70 documents the activity, P129 is about the designed landscape (E27 Site / E24). Each aggregate figure = E13 Attribute Assignment, P14 carried out by the trust (or platform), P140 assigned attribute to the road proposal, P177 assigned property of type 'share of respondents opposed' (E55, a property external to the CRM, licensed by P177's scope note), P141 assigned an E54 Dimension with P90 has value 58 and P91 has unit percent; multiple contradictory assignments simply accumulate, per the Monotonicity section (crm732#s0057). Free-text comments = E33 Linguistic Object with P190 has symbolic content, P67 refers to the landscape. What the CRM genuinely does not give you is a class for 'sentiment' as modelled meaning - the comments stay as symbolic content, not as semantics - but that is a limit on interpretation, not the blanket out-of-scope both answers assert.
reasoning: Both answers correctly reject E16 (P39 measured -> E18 Physical Thing, P40 observed dimension -> E54; verified) and both verify on Issue 580 (CRMsoc discontinued, Bern April 2025) and Issue 581, but both then declare that the aggregate results have 'no structured home in the model', which P177's own scope note and Issue 615's amendment to E13 contradict. Both reject E13 on a constraint that does not exist - anonymity of the *respondents* is irrelevant, since the actor required by P14 is the assertor, and crm732#s0024/#s0046 handle unattributed creation events by defaulting responsibility to the institution; B's 'E13's own scope note frames it around a single identifiable opinion-holder' is an unsupported gloss, and A quotes 'all instances of properties described in a knowledge base are the opinion of someone' verbatim but uses it to mean the opposite of what it says. B edges ahead because it located and quoted verbatim the one piece of normative scope text either answer found (crm732#s0005, the personnel/accounting/visitor-statistics exclusion), whereas A argued mainly from absence of a matching class; B's application of that clause is nonetheless a stretch, since the exclusion is qualified by 'solely for the administration and management of cultural institutions' and a consultation on the fate of the designed landscape documents the site, not the institution's housekeeping.
